paths.description: Homepage and sportsbook listing: entry template, navigation, promotions, event lists and betslip shell.
Representative event detail and market-selection journey.
Primary account-registration form and empty-submit recovery state.
Authentication and account-recovery surface inspected for field assistance and modern auth.

findings.summary: Persistent chrome does not react to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no scroll timeline and the mobile captures show full top and bottom chrome remaining fixed while content space is constrained.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a CSS scroll-state container query or a compacting header pattern so persistent navigation yields space as users scroll.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport breakpoints rather than container-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS inspection found no @container rule or non-normal container type across the representative templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards and panels a containment context and use size container queries where their layout changes independently of the viewport.

findings.summary: Many mobile targets are too small or crowded.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 24 target-size failures on home; mobile screenshot shows dense horizontally clipped card carousels and compact icon/navigation targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive targets and spacing to at least WCAG target-size expectations, while preserving visible :focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: Registration errors are not visibly actionable after an empty submission.
findings.evidence: After an empty JOIN NOW submission, the page showed no visible field errors; the probe found only an empty aria-live=assertive paragraph.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, move focus to the first invalid field, show specific inline messages, set aria-invalid, and announce a concise error summary.

findings.summary: Simulated mobile loading misses the Core Web Vitals performance bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 7.9s, TBT 1,680ms and performance 47. A separate trace was faster but still recorded 241ms TBT, so throttled-device risk is clear.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content, reduce startup JavaScript, delay non-critical integrations, and retest on representative mobile/network conditions.

findings.summary: JavaScript blocks the main thread during startup.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 3.8s main-thread work and 2.7s JS execution; the trace recorded four long tasks, longest 233ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary startup work, split long tasks, schedule non-urgent work after interaction readiness, and move suitable computation off-thread.

findings.summary: The initial dependency chain is broad and includes avoidable blocking work.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 160 requests and 13 stylesheets; Lighthouse estimated 340ms render-blocking savings and flagged the network dependency tree.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, consolidate/defer route styles and scripts, and audit preloads so only truly critical resources receive early priority.

findings.summary: The page ships a large amount of unused and legacy JavaScript.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 1.05MB across 87 script requests. Lighthouse estimated 409KiB unused JavaScript and flagged 32KiB legacy code.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split bundles, remove unconditional polyfills/dependencies, and load casino, analytics and other optional capabilities only when needed.

findings.summary: Accessible names are missing on multiple controls and images.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name, image-alt, link-name and visible-label/accessibility-name matching checks; image inspection found two images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon-only control and link a programmatic name, make visible labels match accessible names, and provide meaningful or empty alt as appropriate.

findings.summary: Landmark and heading structure is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found no main landmark; home has no h1 and the rendered html element has no lang. Help has an h1 but skips through mixed h2/h3 structures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one main landmark, one descriptive page h1 per route, logical heading levels, and verify keyboard focus order and visible focus across all fixed chrome.

findings.summary: Touch target sizing prevents an inclusive mobile experience.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 24 target-size failures on home and 13 on registration, despite correct viewport scaling.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas and spacing without disabling zoom; retest at 200% zoom and 320 CSS px reflow.

findings.summary: Many images lack intrinsic dimensions and use inefficient sizing.
findings.evidence: Image inspection found 8 of 15 images without width/height, 8 oversized, and 9 in legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio for every image and serve correctly sized modern sources through srcset/sizes.

findings.summary: Production diagnostics and browser delivery hygiene are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse join best-practices scored 77 and reported missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript; home also ships legacy JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish secured production source maps for diagnostics and remove avoidable legacy bundles using an explicit Baseline support policy.

findings.summary: Public content is invisible to crawlers that do not execute JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability capture returned 0% rendered-word coverage, isJsShell=true, and crawler view only says to enable JavaScript, despite robots explicitly permitting crawlers.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render or statically generate public sports, help, promotion and editorial content, including title, h1 and description in raw HTML.

findings.summary: Unknown routes return HTTP 200 with self-canonical URLs.
findings.evidence: A deliberately nonexistent route returned HTTP 200, generated a canonical URL and had no noindex directive, although the visual page says it does not exist.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an actual 404 status and either omit canonical metadata or use a suitable noindex policy on not-found responses.

findings.summary: Rich public entities lack structured data.
findings.evidence: Home provides Open Graph metadata but the recon found no JSON-LD for the organization, sporting events, games or articles.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org JSON-LD for Organization and relevant visible entity templates, while retaining the existing social metadata.

findings.summary: Transport protections and cookie policy are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no HSTS or nosniff and CSP only defines frame-ancestors; bp_country is not Secure. Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, nosniff, a restrictive script/style/connect CSP, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure.

findings.summary: Analytics and research integrations create a sizeable third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 382,504 third-party bytes; trackers found GTM, Sentry and Maze across six third-party origins, with GTM accounting for about 355KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory each third party, load non-essential analytics only after appropriate consent/context, minimise payloads, and self-host or remove integrations where practical.

findings.summary: A sensitive account flow relies on passwords without passkey support.
findings.evidence: Login probe found current-password but no WebAuthn/PublicKeyCredential/passkey surface; username/mobile field also lacks a username autocomplete token. No permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in and reauthentication alongside recovery-safe fallback, and add correct username autocomplete semantics.

findings.summary: Core public content does not survive without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: The raw/crawler view contains only an enable-JavaScript notice while the rendered page has 5,006 characters; content coverage is 0%.
findings.suggestedFix: Render core navigation, current event/listing content, help and legal information in HTML, then hydrate betting interactions as an enhancement.

findings.summary: The visual 404 recovery is helpful but the HTTP state is misleading.
findings.evidence: The unknown route offers Browse Events, Home and Help, but the server responds 200 and canonicals the nonexistent URL, so clients and caches cannot distinguish failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the useful recovery UI while returning the correct status and explicit error state to browsers, agents and intermediaries.

findings.summary: The document language is missing across localized pages.
findings.evidence: DOM and Lighthouse both found html lang empty, even though the page declares en-UG hreflang and many country/language variants.
findings.suggestedFix: Set html lang=en-UG (and dir where appropriate) on the server for this locale; ensure every regional variant sets its own BCP 47 language tag.

findings.summary: The installable app has no offline fallback.
findings.evidence: A manifest and active service worker exist, but service-worker source deletes caches on activation and falls through to a plain fetch when offline, with no offline document.
findings.suggestedFix: Precache a minimal offline shell/help page and provide explicit offline/retry states for network-dependent sports data.

findings.summary: Registration validation does not provide clear feedback after submission.
findings.evidence: The empty-submit test produced no visible messages and only an empty assertive live region, leaving the user without a clear correction path.
findings.suggestedFix: Use interaction-timed validation with explicit field messages, aria-invalid/aria-describedby, an announced summary, and focus on the first error.

findings.summary: Account and support forms omit important autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: Join fields for phone, first name, last name and identification number have empty autocomplete; login username is also empty, while only password tokens are set.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply appropriate autocomplete tokens such as username, tel-national, given-name, family-name and current/new-password, avoiding tokens for fields that must not be retained.

findings.summary: Casino imagery is oversized, eager and often legacy-formatted.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 8 oversized, 8 below-fold eager, 9 legacy-format and 8 dimensionless images; several 300-400px assets display at 99px.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive AVIF/WebP sources, reserve dimensions and lazy-load below-fold tiles while keeping only true LCP imagery eager.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts consume a disproportionate part of the page budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties transferred 382KB of a 1.36MB load; GTM alone transferred about 355KB across two script endpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, defer analytics until idle/consent, and remove duplicate or low-value tags.

findings.summary: The initial JavaScript heap is heavy for a listing page.
findings.evidence: Heap summary recorded 1,075,130 nodes and 53.85MB self size. After 10 menu toggles growth was modest (+2,109 nodes, +0.53MB), which does not indicate an obvious repeated-interaction leak but confirms a high baseline.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce always-loaded application state and bundles, virtualise large lists, and profile retained objects on long sportsbook/casino sessions.
